Which solution addresses both concerns effectively?

options.text: Remove all security guardrails to speed up processing time and reduce compute resource consumption.
Deploy the application on self-managed EC2 instances without API rate limiting or input sanitization.
Store all incoming user prompts in an Amazon DynamoDB table with point-in-time recovery enabled.
Configure Amazon Bedrock Guardrails with input validation filters to block prompt injections, and enforce maximum token limits in API requests to control costs.

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provide robust security against prompt injection, while enforcing token limits directly mitigates excessive cost inflation from verbose inputs.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Removing guardrails exposes the application to severe security vulnerabilities such as prompt injection.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Self-managed EC2 instances increase operational overhead and lack built-in prompt defense mechanisms.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Storing prompts in DynamoDB addresses persistence and auditing, but does not actively control token costs or prevent prompt injections.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A healthcare analytics firm is processing clinical trial data using Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs. The jobs run intermittently throughout the month. To adhere to HIPAA compliance and optimize costs, how should the data security and infrastructure be configured?

options.text: Store data in public S3 buckets and use standard on-demand processing instances without encryption.
Encrypt data using AWS KMS, store it in private S3 buckets with VPC endpoints, and use SageMaker processing instances that terminate automatically upon job completion.
Disable AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch logs to reduce logging storage fees.
Keep SageMaker processing instances running 24/7 so that data is immediately ready for analysis at any time.

questions.explanation: Ensuring data is encrypted and processed within secure network boundaries satisfies compliance standards, while spinning up ephemeral processing instances eliminates idle compute costs.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Using public buckets and unencrypted data violates HIPAA compliance regulations.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Disabling logging violates compliance requirements that mandate audit trails for healthcare data processing.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Running processing instances continuously when jobs are intermittent leads to excessive, unnecessary costs.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise AI team is evaluating model deployment options on AWS for a document summarization tool. They want to ensure cost predictability while meeting strict data governance rules that prohibit sending data to third-party endpoints. Which deployment strategy provides the best balance of governance and cost control?

options.text: Store all generated summaries in public Amazon S3 static websites for easy internal sharing.
Use Amazon Bedrock foundation models with AWS PrivateLink to ensure data remains within the AWS network, paying only for tokens consumed.
Route all requests through public internet gateways to third-party external APIs to take advantage of lower promotional pricing.
Deploy models on unmanaged physical servers on-premises and connect via insecure VPN tunnels.

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock accessed via AWS PrivateLink maintains strict data privacy and governance boundaries while offering pay-as-you-go cost structures without idle infrastructure overhead.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Storing summaries in public S3 buckets creates a severe data leak vulnerability.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Routing corporate data over public internet gateways to third-party APIs violates enterprise data governance policies.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Maintaining unmanaged on-premises hardware increases operational burden and infrastructure management costs.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A financial institution is deploying an automated loan approval model on Amazon SageMaker. The risk and compliance committee requires that every model prediction be auditable and reproducible. To manage cloud expenditures efficiently, how should the inference infrastructure be structured?

options.text: Delete all inference logs immediately after generation to save on Amazon S3 storage costs.
Run all inference tasks on single-core development instances without monitoring or scaling policies.
Deploy the model with Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor and enable capture of inference request/response payloads to encrypted S3, utilizing Auto Scaling to manage compute costs.
Avoid using IAM roles and attach AdministratorAccess policies to all SageMaker execution roles for simplicity.

questions.explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor provides necessary auditing capabilities by capturing data payloads securely, while Auto Scaling optimizes infrastructure spend.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Deleting inference logs violates compliance and auditing mandates required for financial models.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Development instances lack the performance and reliability required for production financial workloads.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Using overly permissive IAM policies violates security best practices and compliance frameworks.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An e-commerce company uses an Amazon Bedrock foundation model to generate product descriptions. The marketing team experiences high seasonal volume changes. The chief financial officer requests a cost-control mechanism that prevents unexpected billing spikes while maintaining security guardrails.

options.text: Set up AWS Budgets actions to alert stakeholders and automatically throttle API requests when spending thresholds approach limits, combined with Bedrock Guardrails.
Disable Amazon CloudWatch billing alarms to avoid receiving frequent notification emails.
Migrate all workloads to unencrypted local storage servers with manual script management.
Remove all IAM permissions from the marketing team to prevent them from accessing the application during peak periods.

questions.explanation: AWS Budgets integrated with automated actions provides effective guardrails against unexpected cost overruns, aligning with financial governance standards.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Disabling billing alarms removes vital visibility into cost trends and prevents early detection of spending anomalies.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Moving to unmanaged servers increases security risks and operational costs.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Removing user access halts business operations rather than optimizing costs or managing volume spikes.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A legal technology firm is building an AI contract review tool on AWS. The system processes sensitive legal documents using Amazon Bedrock. Compliance requires data encryption in transit and at rest, and finance requires optimizing costs for low-utilization periods. Which architectural design is correct?

options.text: Disable IAM authentication to allow all internal employees unrestricted access to the contract review endpoints.
Deploy dedicated, high-tier provisioned throughput capacity units that run continuously 24/7 regardless of usage volume.
Use Amazon Bedrock on-demand invocation with data encrypted in transit via TLS and at rest using AWS KMS, scaling to zero when not in use.
Store legal documents in unencrypted public S3 buckets to reduce KMS key management overhead.

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock on-demand usage satisfies cost optimization for fluctuating or low utilization, while standard encryption mechanisms fulfill strict data governance rules.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Disabling IAM authentication violates least-privilege security principles and enterprise governance standards.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Continuous provisioned throughput is expensive and violates cost optimization goals for low-utilization workloads.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Unencrypted public storage violates fundamental legal and security compliance requirements.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An AI engineering team is training a proprietary machine learning model on Amazon SageMaker. Management wants to reduce infrastructure costs during the development phase while ensuring that training data accessed from Amazon S3 is fully secured against interception.

options.text: Disable VPC security groups and allow training instances to communicate over the public internet to bypass NAT gateway fees.
Store all training scripts and datasets unencrypted in publicly accessible Amazon S3 buckets.
Keep SageMaker notebook instances running overnight and over weekends without interruption.
Use SageMaker training jobs with VPC security groups restricting traffic, and leverage Amazon SageMaker Managed Spot Training.

questions.explanation: Combining SageMaker Managed Spot Training with secure VPC configurations achieves significant cost savings while maintaining robust network security.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Bypassing VPC security introduces severe data exposure risks and violates enterprise security policies.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Public S3 buckets expose proprietary training data to unauthorized external entities.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Leaving development notebooks running continuously incurs unnecessary idle charges.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A multinational corporation is deploying generative AI assistants across multiple business units using Amazon Bedrock. The governance board requires strict cost allocation tagging and security auditing across all AI API calls. How should the cloud architect implement these controls?

options.text: Disable AWS CloudTrail across all accounts to reduce log storage fees and simplify management overhead.
Rely solely on manual monthly spreadsheet tracking for all AI prompt costs without using native AWS tagging.
Tag all Amazon Bedrock resources and API requests using AWS Cost Allocation Tags, enable AWS CloudTrail data events for Bedrock, and use AWS IAM for access control.
Share a single root AWS account and a single IAM user credential among all business units to simplify billing management.

questions.explanation: AWS Cost Allocation Tags and CloudTrail data events provide the necessary granularity for financial tracking and security auditing across multi-unit AI deployments.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Disabling CloudTrail violates security governance mandates by removing auditing capabilities.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Manual spreadsheet tracking does not scale and lacks the precision required for enterprise cloud financial management.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Sharing root accounts and credentials violates core AWS security best practices and prevents accurate cost attribution.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise deployment of an Amazon Bedrock foundation model spans the us-east-1 and us-west-2 regions to achieve high availability. The site reliability engineering team needs to design a disaster recovery strategy that minimizes Recovery Time Objective (RTO) while controlling costs. Which multi-region architectural pattern is best suited for this requirement?

options.text: Deploy a warm standby architecture where the secondary region runs inference requests at full capacity continuously to ensure instant data synchronization.
Maintain an active-active setup using Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing with automated health checks targeting Amazon Bedrock endpoints in both regions.
Utilize a cold backup model where Amazon Bedrock foundation models are invoked in the secondary region only after an alarm triggers a manual infrastructure deployment via AWS CloudFormation.
Configure cross-region replication of Amazon SageMaker model artifacts to continuously retrain and hot-swap weights in the secondary region.

questions.explanation: For stateless generative AI applications using managed services like Amazon Bedrock, an active-active multi-region architecture combined with DNS-level routing (such as Route 53 latency-based routing with health checks) offers the lowest RTO and optimal resource utilization.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Running a warm standby at full capacity duplicates costs unnecessarily, defeating the cost-control objective while providing marginal benefit over active-active for stateless LLM calls.
wrongOptionNotes.C: A cold backup introduces significant RTO due to the manual intervention and deployment time required during an outage, failing the minimal RTO requirement.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Amazon Bedrock manages underlying foundation models without exposing weight files for customer-managed cross-region replication, making this approach technically inapplicable.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A global financial organization is deploying a customer-facing AI assistant powered by Amazon SageMaker Real-Time Inference endpoints across two AWS regions. To satisfy business continuity mandates, the system must fail over automatically if the primary region suffers a complete outage. How should the team configure cross-region resilience for the SageMaker endpoints?

options.text: Set up a primary SageMaker endpoint with an active failover target pointing to an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group running open-source models.
Configure an Amazon API Gateway multi-region deployment with AWS Lambda proxy integration that automatically synchronizes stateful inference sessions across regions.
Rely solely on Amazon CloudFront origin failover to redirect HTTP 5xx errors from the primary SageMaker endpoint URL to the secondary region endpoint URL.

Deploy identical SageMaker endpoints in both regions, front them with an Amazon Route 53 DNS routing policy featuring weighted records and health checks, and ensure model artifacts are version-controlled via Amazon S3 cross-region replication.

questions.explanation: Resilience for SageMaker real-time endpoints across multiple regions requires parallel deployments managed by intelligent DNS routing (Route 53) with health checks, supported by synchronized model artifacts.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Mixing managed SageMaker endpoints with unmanaged EC2 instances introduces architectural drift, inconsistent inference behavior, and complex operational overhead.
wrongOptionNotes.B: SageMaker inference endpoints are stateless, and synchronizing stateful LLM conversational sessions across regions requires external session stores like Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables rather than Lambda proxy integration alone.
wrongOptionNotes.C: CloudFront origin failover is designed for static assets and web servers; it lacks deep health integration and payload parsing required for robust machine learning inference endpoint recovery.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A multinational enterprise is building a compliance auditing tool using Amazon Bedrock. The architecture requires resilient failover between two AWS regions to prevent downtime during regional network partitions. When evaluating disaster recovery for foundation model invocations, what is a critical architectural consideration regarding data governance?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock automatically synchronizes chat history across all global regions to ensure zero data loss during a failover event.
Disaster recovery failover for foundation models requires manual database migrations of vector embeddings stored in Amazon OpenSearch Service.
Cross-region failover may route sensitive inference payloads to a secondary region that lacks compliance certification or violates data residency requirements.
Cross-region model invocations are prohibited by AWS shared responsibility model unless a dedicated AWS Direct Connect link is established.

questions.explanation: Multi-region AI disaster recovery must carefully balance technical failover capabilities against legal and regulatory data residency boundaries to avoid compliance breaches.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Amazon Bedrock does not automatically synchronize customer conversational history or prompt logs across disparate AWS regions.
wrongOptionNotes.B: While vector databases must be replicated, this addresses data persistence rather than the core governance and regional boundary risks associated with inference processing.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS does not require Direct Connect for cross-region API calls; standard encrypted public or VPC endpoint connectivity is fully supported.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An AI-powered document processing platform runs on Amazon SageMaker asynchronous inference endpoints in the primary region. The engineering team wants to establish a disaster recovery plan that guarantees data durability and operational continuity for unprocessed payload requests during a regional disaster. Which strategy best meets this goal?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 cross-region replication for input and output S3 buckets associated with asynchronous endpoints, paired with secondary SageMaker asynchronous endpoints configured to poll the replica buckets upon DNS failover.
Establish a cross-region AWS Lambda function that reads memory dumps from failing SageMaker instances and replays them.
Rely on Amazon CloudWatch alarms to trigger manual re-submission of failed API requests from client applications.
Configure Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoints in the secondary region with an active-passive load balancer to capture dropped TCP connections.

questions.explanation: SageMaker Asynchronous Inference leverages Amazon S3 for request and response storage. Combining S3 cross-region replication with standby asynchronous endpoints in the recovery region guarantees durability and seamless processing recovery.

wrongOptionNotes.B: SageMaker instance memory is volatile and inaccessible for direct dumping; this approach is technically unfeasible.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Relying on manual client-side re-submission increases RTO and introduces poor user experience, failing enterprise disaster recovery requirements.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Real-time endpoints do not natively queue large payloads or handle asynchronous batch processing tasks effectively compared to asynchronous inference endpoints.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A cloud architecture team is designing a multi-region disaster recovery framework for an enterprise generative AI application using Amazon Bedrock. Management requires a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of zero for user preference profiles and conversational metadata, while accepting an RTO of under one minute for inference continuity. Which database and routing combination should the team implement?

options.text: Amazon RDS PostgreSQL with asynchronous read replicas and manual DNS switchover scripts.
Amazon Aurora multi-master clusters with Amazon CloudFront custom origin failover rules.
Amazon S3 Standard storage with cross-region replication and standard Route 53 latency routing.
Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables for data persistence paired with Amazon Route 53 application recovery controller for routing AI inference traffic.

questions.explanation: Achieving an RPO of zero for metadata requires multi-master storage solutions like DynamoDB Global Tables, while sub-minute RTO for routing requires advanced DNS control mechanisms like Route 53 Application Recovery Controller.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Asynchronous read replicas introduce a non-zero RPO during regional failures, and manual DNS switchover scripts cannot guarantee a sub-minute RTO.
wrongOptionNotes.B: While Aurora multi-master supports low RPO, CloudFront origin failover is sub-optimal for managing dynamic API calls to AI inference backends compared to dedicated DNS recovery controllers.
wrongOptionNotes.C: S3 is not optimized for transactional, low-latency conversational metadata updates required by real-time AI user profile applications.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An AI platform team is reviewing the multi-region resilience of their custom model training pipeline hosted on Amazon SageMaker. They want to ensure that if a regional outage occurs during a multi-day distributed training job, checkpoints stored in Amazon S3 can be used to resume training in a secondary region with minimal wasted compute time. What is the most resilient design pattern?

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 cross-region replication for the training checkpoint bucket, and build automated validation scripts in the secondary region to resume SageMaker training jobs from the latest replicated checkpoint.
Configure an active-active SageMaker training cluster that synchronizes gradient updates across regions in real-time over the public internet.
Use Amazon EBS snapshot replication to copy the training instance root volumes to the secondary region every hour.
Rely on AWS Backup to automatically fail over active training jobs and spin up identical GPU clusters in the recovery region.

questions.explanation: For distributed machine learning training, resilience relies on frequent application-level checkpointing to Amazon S3, S3 cross-region replication, and orchestration scripts that resume training from the last saved state.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Real-time synchronous gradient updates across cross-region networks suffer from extreme latency bottlenecks, rendering distributed training inefficient or entirely stalled.
wrongOptionNotes.C: EBS snapshots capture instance block storage rather than distributed training state files, and training frameworks typically save application-level checkpoints to Amazon S3.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS Backup does not natively orchestrate active cross-region failover and resumption of in-flight distributed machine learning training jobs.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A financial services firm runs an automated fraud-detection system using Amazon SageMaker endpoints deployed across two AWS regions. The risk management team mandates that if the primary region's endpoint experiences elevated error rates, traffic must fail over automatically without violating compliance rules regarding cross-border data transfer. How should the team configure the health monitoring and routing?

options.text: Implement Amazon Route 53 health checks configured to probe the SageMaker endpoint invocation status, automatically routing traffic to the compliant secondary region only when failure thresholds are breached.
Rely on client-side retry logic with randomized exponential backoff to hammer the primary endpoint until recovery occurs.
Use AWS Shield Advanced to automatically reroute traffic during a regional hardware failure.
Configure an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) in the primary region to directly proxy failing requests to an ELB in an unrestricted international AWS region.

questions.explanation: Automated DNS health checks via Amazon Route 53 provide reliable, policy-compliant traffic redirection away from failing AI inference endpoints to designated recovery regions.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Client-side retry loops exacerbate regional outages, increase latency, and fail to provide true disaster recovery failover.
wrongOptionNotes.C: AWS Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks, not regional infrastructure outages or application-level inference failures.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Routing traffic to an unrestricted international region violates compliance mandates regarding data residency and cross-border transfer restrictions.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise deploying large language models via Amazon Bedrock needs to plan for potential regional service degradations. The chief information security officer (CISO) requires that all disaster recovery failover mechanisms maintain strict encryption in transit and at rest using customer-managed AWS KMS keys. What is the key configuration requirement for multi-region Bedrock resilience?

options.text: Provision multi-region AWS KMS keys or matching customer-managed keys in both the primary and secondary regions so that replicated payloads and model logs can be decrypted securely during failover.
Rely entirely on AWS managed keys because they automatically replicate encryption material globally without user configuration.
Disable encryption during disaster recovery scenarios to reduce latency overhead during failover transition.
Store the decryption keys exclusively in the primary region and use secure tunneling to process data in the secondary region.

questions.explanation: Maintaining strict security postures during multi-region disaster recovery requires properly configured multi-region or corresponding customer-managed KMS keys in all operational regions.

wrongOptionNotes.B: While AWS managed keys simplify encryption, compliance mandates often specifically require customer-managed keys (CMKs) with explicit multi-region replication controls.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Disabling encryption violates core enterprise security policies and regulatory compliance standards under all operational conditions.
wrongOptionNotes.D: If the primary region is experiencing an outage, a dependency on primary-region key infrastructure will cause decryption and failover to fail completely.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A digital media company is building a generative AI content creation suite using Amazon Bedrock. The platform must survive a total regional outage of us-east-1 without data loss or user session interruption. The engineering team implements Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables and configures multi-region application routing. During a simulated failover test, users report that their active chat sessions are lost. What architectural element was missing from the disaster recovery design?

options.text: Increasing the AWS Lambda execution timeout limit to 15 minutes.
Cross-region replication of Amazon CloudWatch log groups for real-time debugging.
Stateless application tier design where session tokens or identifiers stored in the global database are referenced by client applications rather than holding local server memory state.
Enabling Amazon EBS volume encryption with multi-region keys.

questions.explanation: Seamless failover for conversational AI applications requires a completely stateless application layer that persists session identifiers and context in globally replicated databases.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Lambda timeouts govern function execution duration, not session state persistence across regional failures.
wrongOptionNotes.B: CloudWatch log replication aids observability and troubleshooting, but does not impact end-user session state preservation.
wrongOptionNotes.D: EBS encryption protects block storage data at rest but does not manage dynamic user conversational session states.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An insurance corporation is architecting a high-availability AI pipeline on AWS using Amazon SageMaker. The architecture must ensure that if a primary inference instance fails, traffic is automatically routed to healthy instances within the same region, while simultaneously preparing for a wider cross-region disaster. Which combination of features provides this layered resilience?

options.text: Amazon CloudFront pointing directly to SageMaker container IP addresses.
Single-instance SageMaker endpoints managed by AWS Auto Scaling groups without an Elastic Load Balancer.

SageMaker multi-instance real-time endpoints behind an internal Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) for local high availability, combined with Amazon Route 53 health checks for cross-region disaster recovery.
Relying on AWS IAM policies to switch resource ownership during an outage.

questions.explanation: Layered resilience requires local load balancing and instance redundancy (ELB and multi-instance endpoints) coupled with global DNS-based failover (Route 53) for regional disaster recovery.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Directly pointing CloudFront to dynamic container IPs bypasses load balancing and health checks, leading to severe availability failures.
wrongOptionNotes.B: SageMaker endpoints manage their own underlying instances; attaching raw Auto Scaling groups directly without an ELB or native endpoint scaling is architecturally incorrect.
wrongOptionNotes.D: IAM policies define permissions and access control, not traffic routing or instance-level failover.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise AI governance team is auditing their multi-region disaster recovery posture for Amazon Bedrock deployments. They discover that while foundation model inference endpoints are deployed in both us-east-1 and us-west-2, custom fine-tuned model weights (custom models) created via Bedrock are only present in us-east-1. What is the operational risk of this configuration during a primary region failure?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock automatically synchronizes all custom model weights across all AWS regions in the background within 60 seconds.
The application will automatically fall back to the base foundation model without any loss in domain-specific accuracy.
The failover will succeed seamlessly because foundation models and fine-tuned weights are stored globally by default.

Applications failing over to us-west-2 will be unable to invoke the custom fine-tuned model because custom model resources are region-specific and must be explicitly copied or trained in the secondary region.

questions.explanation: Custom fine-tuned models in Amazon Bedrock are region-specific assets. Comprehensive multi-region disaster recovery requires multi-region training or explicit model copying strategies.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Bedrock does not automatically synchronize customer fine-tuned model artifacts across disparate AWS regions.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Falling back to a base model bypasses fine-tuning, which will significantly degrade domain-specific model accuracy and application performance.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Fine-tuned models contain proprietary customer data and are stored locally within the AWS region where the training job was executed.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A global logistics provider is implementing disaster recovery for a fleet of edge-connected AI inference processors that sync data back to AWS. The central cloud backend utilizes Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock. During network disconnects, edge devices must continue operating locally. When connectivity is restored, how should the architecture reconcile queued inference logs without overwhelming the primary region?

options.text: Disable logging at the edge during network outages and discard un-synced records permanently.
Route all edge traffic directly through Amazon CloudFront static distribution points.
Use Amazon SQS queues with exponential backoff and dead-letter queues at the ingestion boundary to gracefully buffer and throttle incoming data synchronization from edge devices.
Configure edge devices to stream logs directly to Amazon Bedrock inference endpoints in an active-active global mesh.

questions.explanation: Buffering unpredictable traffic surges resulting from post-outage reconnections requires managed queuing services like Amazon SQS with throttling and backoff controls.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Discarding inference logs violates compliance and auditing mandates that require complete traceability of AI processing.
wrongOptionNotes.B: CloudFront is optimized for content delivery and web caching, not durable queuing of asynchronous operational logs from edge devices.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Bedrock inference endpoints process real-time prompt requests and are not designed to ingest raw, batched edge synchronization logs.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A financial technology company is designing a cross-region disaster recovery architecture for an Amazon SageMaker batch transform pipeline. The pipeline processes millions of customer records nightly. If the primary region fails mid-job, the system must resume processing with minimal data duplication. What is the recommended design pattern?

options.text: Maintain an active duplicate batch transform job running simultaneously in the secondary region processing the exact same data.
Rely on Amazon EBS volume mirroring between regions to hot-swap batch processing nodes.
Rerun the entire multi-hour batch transform job from scratch in the secondary region as soon as a CloudWatch alarm triggers.

Partition input datasets into discrete, idempotent chunks stored in Amazon S3 with cross-region replication, tracking processing state in a DynamoDB Global Table so secondary workers pick up unprocessed chunks.

questions.explanation: Efficient multi-region batch processing disaster recovery depends on data partitioning, idempotent workloads, and centralized state tracking via DynamoDB.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Running duplicate high-throughput batch jobs simultaneously doubles costs unnecessarily and creates race conditions on output storage.
wrongOptionNotes.B: EBS volumes cannot be attached across different AWS regions, making cross-region volume mirroring impossible.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Rerunning entire large-scale batch jobs from scratch wastes significant compute time and fails to optimize recovery efficiency.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise deploying a mission-critical AI customer service agent using Amazon Bedrock is establishing a multi-region failover strategy. The risk committee mandates that the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) must be under 5 seconds, and automated failover must not cause split-brain data corruption in user chat histories. Which design fulfills these criteria?

options.text: An active-passive setup using Amazon RDS read replicas with synchronous cross-region replication.
Direct IP failover using Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routing across arbitrary public cloud providers.

An active-passive multi-region architecture managed by Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller with health checks, backed by Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables for single-digit second failover and zero data corruption.
Active-active multi-region deployment with manual DNS record updates performed by the on-call engineering team.

questions.explanation: Meeting ultra-low RTO targets alongside data integrity requires specialized routing controllers like Route 53 ARC and globally consistent datastores like DynamoDB Global Tables.

wrongOptionNotes.A: RDS does not support synchronous cross-region replication; cross-region replication in RDS is always asynchronous.
wrongOptionNotes.B: BGP announcements across cloud providers are complex, error-prone, and do not integrate natively with managed AWS AI services like Amazon Bedrock.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Manual DNS updates take several minutes or hours, failing the strict sub-5-second RTO requirement.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A healthcare analytics organization is reviewing the disaster recovery and resilience posture of its generative AI workflows running on Amazon SageMaker. The architecture handles protected health information (PHI). During a multi-region failover drill, the security team notes that diagnostic logs from SageMaker model invocations were temporarily exposed during transit across regions. How should the team remediate this vulnerability?

options.text: Disable all logging during disaster recovery drills to avoid compliance review.

Ensure that all inter-region traffic utilizes AWS PrivateLink or encrypted VPC peering connections, and verify that CloudWatch log streams are encrypted using customer-managed KMS keys in both regions.
Route all cross-region diagnostic logging through public HTTP endpoints with basic authentication headers.
Rely on default S3 bucket policies without encryption because internal AWS networks are inherently secure.

questions.explanation: Handling sensitive data like PHI during disaster recovery requires strict adherence to encryption-in-transit (PrivateLink) and encryption-at-rest (KMS) across all participating regions.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Disabling audit and diagnostic logging violates mandatory compliance and traceability controls for healthcare workloads.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Public HTTP endpoints violate healthcare compliance standards (such as HIPAA) for transmitting protected health information.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Assuming underlying network security without explicit encryption and access controls fails enterprise compliance standards for PHI data.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A defense contractor is processing classified documents using Amazon Bedrock foundation models. To comply with strict data sovereignty mandates, the security team must ensure that no customer inputs or model outputs are retained for any purpose by the service provider, even for product improvement. How should the solutions architect configure this?

options.text: Configure AWS Key Management Service (KMS) customer managed keys with automatic annual rotation to encrypt all ephemeral inference cache.
Opt out of model training using the Amazon Bedrock console or APIs, which ensures AWS and its model providers do not use customer data to train or improve models.
Enable AWS CloudTrail data events to capture all inference payloads and route them to an encrypted S3 bucket for local retention while blocking Bedrock logging.
Deploy the model exclusively on dedicated Amazon SageMaker instances instead of Amazon Bedrock to prevent multi-tenant data logging.

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock offers data privacy by default, ensuring customer data is never used to train foundational models. Organizations can explicitly opt out of any potential human review or data logging programs via the Bedrock data privacy settings to meet strict regulatory frameworks.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Encryption keys protect data at rest, but they do not control whether a service provider retains inference logs for model improvement.
wrongOptionNotes.C: CloudTrail does not capture full prompt and response payloads for Bedrock invocations, and storing them locally violates the requirement of handling raw inputs without provider retention.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Amazon Bedrock provides the same strict data privacy controls and zero-retention policies when training is opted out, making migration to SageMaker unnecessary.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise is setting up automated model evaluation pipelines in Amazon Bedrock. The security architect wants to ensure that evaluation jobs running against proprietary foundation models comply with corporate policies restricting data export outside the designated AWS account. Where are the automated evaluation results and generated reports stored by default?

options.text: In Amazon SageMaker Model Registry as part of the model lineage metadata.
In Amazon CloudWatch Logs under the /aws/bedrock/evaluations log group.
In an internal, AWS-managed service bucket owned by the Bedrock foundational model provider, requiring cross-account IAM trust policies.
In an Amazon S3 bucket specified by the user within their own AWS account during the creation of the evaluation job.

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock model evaluation jobs require a designated Amazon S3 bucket within the customer's AWS account to store all input datasets, model response outputs, and comprehensive evaluation reports, ensuring complete data governance and ownership.

wrongOptionNotes.A: SageMaker Model Registry is separate from Amazon Bedrock model evaluation workflows.
wrongOptionNotes.B: CloudWatch logs operational metrics, but detailed model evaluation results and report artifacts are written directly to Amazon S3.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Model providers do not store evaluation outputs in their own accounts; customer data remains strictly within the customer's perimeter.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A financial services company is implementing guardrails for Amazon Bedrock to filter out hate speech, insults, and prompt injection attacks from customer queries. The compliance officer wants to audit all blocked requests. Which AWS service integrates natively with Bedrock Guardrails to capture and alert on policy violations?

options.text: Amazon Macie automated data discovery jobs
AWS Trusted Advisor automated security checks
AWS Shield Advanced DDoS mitigation metrics
Amazon CloudWatch and AWS CloudTrail

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails integrates with CloudWatch and CloudTrail to log blocked prompts, denied responses, and specific filter thresholds triggered during runtime, allowing security teams to build robust auditing and incident response workflows.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 buckets, whereas Bedrock Guardrails handles real-time text evaluation during runtime inference.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Trusted Advisor provides general cloud environment best practice checks, not real-time content filtering telemetry for generative AI.
wrongOptionNotes.C: AWS Shield protects against network and transport layer DDoS attacks, not application-layer prompt injection or content moderation.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A healthcare provider is training a custom clinical model using Amazon SageMaker. The compliance team mandates that all data passing through training jobs, hosting endpoints, and S3 staging buckets must be encrypted using keys controlled entirely by the organization. Which mechanism satisfies this requirement?

options.text: Enabling IAM resource policies on the SageMaker execution role to restrict who can read the training logs.
Using AWS Key Management Service (KMS) customer managed keys (CMKs) configured across SageMaker training jobs, model artifacts, and S3 buckets.
Deploying the SageMaker endpoint inside a public subnet with an Application Load Balancer terminating SSL.
Relying on AWS managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) combined with TLS 1.3 in-transit encryption.

questions.explanation: To meet strict compliance mandates for data encryption at rest, organizations must configure AWS KMS Customer Managed Keys (CMKs) across all SageMaker components, including training input volumes, model output S3 buckets, and inference endpoints.

wrongOptionNotes.A: IAM policies control access permissions but do not encrypt data at rest.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Network perimeter controls do not provide encryption at rest or satisfy customer-managed key requirements.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS managed keys are controlled by AWS rather than the customer, failing the strict requirement for customer-controlled keys.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise is deploying an AI-powered code generator using Amazon Bedrock across multiple business units. The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) requires that unauthorized IAM principals cannot invoke specific high-capability foundation models, regardless of whether they have general Bedrock access. What is the most effective preventative control?

options.text: Attach an AWS WAF web ACL to the Amazon Bedrock API endpoint to filter requests based on IAM token headers.
Apply AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) or resource-based policies to deny bedrock:InvokeModel on specific model ARNs for unauthorized roles.
Configure Amazon GuardDuty to automatically terminate IAM sessions that attempt unauthorized model invocations.
Rely on Amazon Bedrock application logging to detect unauthorized usage after the fact and alert administrators.

questions.explanation: Preventative governance for foundational model access is best enforced using IAM policies and AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) that target the bedrock:InvokeModel API action and restrict access to authorized model ARNs.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS WAF protects public web applications and API Gateway endpoints, not the native Bedrock service APIs directly.
wrongOptionNotes.C: GuardDuty is a detective control that identifies threats, whereas SCPs and IAM policies provide preventative governance.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Logging is a detective control and does not prevent unauthorized execution.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A financial technology company is building a document processing workflow on AWS using Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. The documents contain highly sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII). The compliance team requires that PII must be automatically scrubbed before documents are embedded and stored in the vector database. How should this be achieved?

options.text: Rely on the foundational model's built-in safety filters to ignore PII during embedding generation.
Configure Amazon S3 Object Lambda to automatically remove PII whenever vector search queries are executed.
Enable Amazon Bedrock Guardrails on the vector database storage volume to encrypt PII at rest.
Integrate Amazon Comprehend or a custom data redaction step in the data ingestion pipeline before storing chunks in the vector store.

questions.explanation: Data governance for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) requires sanitizing sensitive data before it reaches vector databases. Implementing an upstream preprocessing step using services like Amazon Comprehend ensures PII is removed prior to embedding creation.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Embedding models generate vector representations of text without automatically masking or redacting PII.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Vector search queries retrieve chunks from the vector database, not directly via S3 Object Lambda during runtime retrieval.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Bedrock Guardrails operate on runtime prompts and model responses, not vector storage volumes, and encryption does not scrub PII.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An AI startup is deploying an Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoint that processes sensitive biometric data. The architecture must comply with data exfiltration prevention standards. How should the security architect configure the VPC environment for the endpoint?

options.text: Rely on security groups with inbound rules restricted to the specific corporate IP address range.
Deploy the endpoint in a public subnet protected by an Internet Gateway and enforce mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication.
Deploy the SageMaker endpoint in a private subnet with no internet gateway, and use VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) for all communications.
Attach a NAT Gateway to the private subnet to mask internal IP addresses during external API callbacks.

questions.explanation: Isolating machine learning endpoints in private subnets without internet access and leveraging AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoints) prevents data exfiltration and ensures secure, internal-only communication.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Security groups control traffic flow but do not prevent outbound data leakage if internal components can reach the public internet.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Public subnets expose resources to the internet, violating standard data exfiltration prevention controls for sensitive biometric data.
wrongOptionNotes.D: A NAT Gateway allows outbound internet access, which contradicts the requirement to prevent data exfiltration.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise machine learning team is collaborating with an external third-party vendor to fine-tune a model on Amazon SageMaker. The vendor requires access to the training dataset, but corporate policy forbids sharing raw S3 buckets externally. What is the most secure architectural approach?

options.text: Make the S3 bucket public with read-only permissions and obfuscate the bucket URL.
Use AWS Lake Formation with fine-grained access control and IAM condition keys to grant the vendor temporary, audited access restricted to specific columns and rows.
Disable encryption on the S3 bucket so the vendor can download the data using standard unencrypted HTTP requests.
Create an IAM user with administrative credentials and share the password securely via email with the vendor's lead engineer.

questions.explanation: AWS Lake Formation provides advanced fine-grained access control, enabling secure data collaboration without exposing raw S3 storage buckets or violating enterprise data-sharing governance policies.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Making S3 buckets public creates a major data leak vulnerability and violates compliance standards.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Disabling encryption exposes data in transit and at rest, failing mandatory security baselines.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Sharing static credentials via insecure channels is a severe security anti-pattern and violates basic access management policies.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An internal audit discovers that developers are deploying Amazon Bedrock models with varying configurations across multiple AWS accounts, leading to governance drift. The security board mandates a centralized mechanism to enforce standard guardrails and prevent unapproved model parameters across the entire enterprise. How should this be implemented?

options.text: Configure Amazon Inspector to scan running EC2 instances for unauthorized Python scripts invoking Bedrock.
Use AWS Control Tower and AWS Organizations to deploy centralized Service Control Policies and standardized Terraform/CloudFormation templates with baseline Bedrock configurations.
Migrate all workloads into a single AWS account so that the root user can monitor all Bedrock activity manually.
Send automated weekly reminder emails to developers instructing them to update their Bedrock configurations manually.

questions.explanation: Enterprise-wide AI governance requires multi-account management strategies using AWS Organizations, SCPs, and standardized Infrastructure as Code templates to enforce compliance baselines automatically.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Inspector scans host vulnerabilities and network reachability, not Bedrock model configurations or multi-account governance policies.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Consolidating all enterprise workloads into a single account violates AWS multi-account best practices and security isolation principles.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Manual reminders rely on human compliance and do not enforce automated organizational guardrails.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A financial institution is implementing Amazon Bedrock for automated customer service. The risk management team mandates that all user prompts and model responses must be inspected for toxic content, and any violations must generate an immediate security incident alert. Which combination of services provides this capability?

options.text: Amazon GuardDuty configured with malicious IP protection for Amazon Bedrock API endpoints.
AWS Trusted Advisor checks combined with AWS Shield Standard.
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails configured with content filters, integrated with Amazon CloudWatch alarms and Amazon SNS to trigger alerts.
AWS WAF integrated with AWS Lambda to inspect incoming HTTP POST requests for toxic keywords before they reach Bedrock.

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provide native content filtering for harmful categories. By pairing Guardrails with Amazon CloudWatch metrics and Amazon SNS, organizations can establish real-time alerting for policy violations.

wrongOptionNotes.A: GuardDuty detects threat intellectual property and compromised credentials, not semantic toxicity within prompt-response payloads.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Neither service evaluates AI model content safety or generates alerts for toxic language.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS WAF operates at the edge for web applications and cannot natively evaluate the semantic toxicity of LLM prompts or generated responses.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An AI development team is configuring fine-tuning jobs for custom foundation models in Amazon Bedrock. They need to ensure that the training datasets stored in Amazon S3 are protected against unauthorized tampering or accidental deletion during the multi-week training cycle. What is the recommended security configuration?

options.text: Disable bucket logging and make the S3 bucket read-only for all external IAM users.
Store training datasets on ephemeral EBS volumes attached to Amazon EC2 instances instead of Amazon S3.
Rely on Amazon CloudWatch to delete any unauthorized modifications to training datasets automatically.
Enable S3 Versioning, configure S3 Object Lock in compliance mode, and enforce strict bucket policies denying delete actions.

questions.explanation: Ensuring data integrity for machine learning training datasets requires immutable storage patterns. Amazon S3 Object Lock and S3 Versioning prevent data tampering or accidental deletion, satisfying model reproducibility and governance requirements.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Disabling logging reduces visibility, and making buckets read-only can block the training job's write requirements for staging outputs.
wrongOptionNotes.B: EBS volumes attached to EC2 are not designed for durable multi-week distributed model training storage compared to S3.
wrongOptionNotes.C: CloudWatch is a monitoring service and cannot automatically modify or revert changes to S3 object data.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A global media corporation is deploying a generative AI application on AWS. The compliance department requires that all access to Amazon Bedrock APIs must be logged with user-level attribution, specifying which internal employee submitted each prompt. How should this auditing requirement be met?

options.text: Attach an AWS WAF rate-based rule to the Amazon Bedrock console.
Ensure that internal applications authenticate users via AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) and pass role sessions, capturing identity details in AWS CloudTrail management events.
Rely on Amazon VPC flow logs to extract employee usernames from network packet headers.
Write custom application code that logs raw user passwords into Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records API calls and related events made by or on behalf of an AWS account. Integrating corporate identity providers via IAM Identity Center ensures that CloudTrail logs contain verifiable user-level attribution for Bedrock invocations.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS WAF manages rate limiting and web exploits, not user identity attribution for API auditing.
wrongOptionNotes.C: VPC flow logs capture IP metadata and network traffic statistics, not application-level user identities.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Logging plaintext passwords or sensitive credentials is a critical security vulnerability and violates compliance standards.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise is establishing a Center of Excellence for generative AI. The governance board mandates that no model deployment in Amazon SageMaker or Amazon Bedrock can proceed without a documented security review. Which AWS service can be used to track compliance status, policies, and evidence centrally across all AI projects?

options.text: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Shield
AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Audit Manager

questions.explanation: AWS Audit Manager simplifies the process of auditing AWS workloads by automating evidence collection and mapping cloud telemetry to standard compliance frameworks, supporting governance boards in AI deployments.

wrongOptionNotes.A: GuardDuty is a threat detection service, not a compliance management framework.
wrongOptionNotes.B: AWS Shield is focused on DDoS protection.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Trusted Advisor provides automated cost, performance, and security checks, but does not manage custom compliance evidence or audit workflows.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A financial firm is building a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) application using Amazon Bedrock and OpenSearch Serverless. The security team discovers that users are able to query documents they are not authorized to view. How should the architecture be remediated to enforce strict document-level access control?

options.text: Disable encryption in transit between Amazon Bedrock and OpenSearch so permission tokens can be evaluated.
Deploy a separate OpenSearch Serverless collection for every individual user in the enterprise.
Rely on Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to block unauthorized keywords dynamically at runtime.
Implement metadata filtering during the vector search query in Bedrock, passing user permission tags retrieved from the authentication layer to restrict retrieved chunks.

questions.explanation: In enterprise RAG architectures, document-level security is enforced by attaching user permission metadata to vector chunks and applying dynamic metadata filters during similarity searches.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Disabling encryption compromises data security in transit and does not solve authorization enforcement.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Maintaining individual collections for every user is operationally unfeasible, expensive, and scales poorly.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Guardrails filter toxic or sensitive content based on text patterns, not user-specific authorization permissions for document retrieval.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An AI engineering team is preparing to deploy an open-source Large Language Model on an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint. The security architect requires that the container executing the model runs with least privilege, preventing any potential container escape from gaining root access to the host. How should this be configured?

options.text: Attach the AWS managed AdministratorAccess policy to the SageMaker execution role to ensure all libraries install correctly.
Disable Amazon VPC integration to allow the container direct internet access for patch updates.
Enable public accessibility on the SageMaker endpoint so the security team can perform remote vulnerability scans.
Configure the SageMaker model container to run with a non-root user and ensure the execution role follows least privilege principles.

questions.explanation: Container security best practices for Amazon SageMaker require configuring containers to execute under non-root user IDs and provisioning least-privilege IAM execution roles to mitigate container escape vulnerabilities.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Attaching AdministratorAccess violates the principle of least privilege.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Disabling VPC integration removes network isolation controls and increases security exposure.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Making endpoints public increases attack surface and violates cloud security best practices.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise is deploying an internal customer support assistant using Amazon Bedrock. Security operations reports that raw PII (Personally Identifiable Information) such as social security numbers are appearing unmasked in model inference response logs stored in Amazon CloudWatch. Which remediation step directly addresses this compliance violation while preserving model functionality?

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 bucket policies on the CloudWatch log export destination to encrypt all stored objects with customer-managed AWS KMS keys.
Modify the Amazon SageMaker model container entrypoint to run a local regex scanner before streaming responses back to clients.
Apply AWS WAF rules in front of the Bedrock API calls to inspect response payloads for regular expressions matching PII and drop matching packets.
Configure Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to detect and redact or block PII entities in both model inputs and outputs.

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails enables organizations to implement safeguards tailored to application requirements and responsible AI policies. It supports content filters, denied words, contextual grounding checks, and PII masking for both user inputs and model responses.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Encryption at rest protects stored data from unauthorized physical or API-level access, but it does not prevent unmasked PII from appearing inside the logs.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Amazon Bedrock is a managed service utilizing foundational models, not a self-hosted SageMaker endpoint where container entrypoints can be modified.
wrongOptionNotes.C: AWS WAF operates at the HTTP request layer and inspects incoming headers and body parameters, but it cannot inspect or modify outbound response payloads from Amazon Bedrock.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A financial institution is training custom credit risk models using Amazon SageMaker. During an audit, compliance discovers that training job logs contain unencrypted intermediate model artifacts and temporary evaluation datasets stored on the default EBS volumes attached to training instances. How should the ML engineers fix this issue?

options.text: Configure the SageMaker TrainingJob API request to specify an AWS KMS key and enable encryption on the ML storage volume.
Enable Amazon GuardDuty across the AWS account to automatically detect unencrypted EBS volumes and re-encrypt them in place.
Route all SageMaker training traffic through an AWS Network Firewall to scrub unencrypted artifacts in transit.
Attach an AWS Shield Advanced protection group to the SageMaker VPC subnet hosting the training instances.

questions.explanation: When running training jobs on Amazon SageMaker, data on the ML storage volumes can be secured by providing a customer-managed AWS KMS key in the training job configuration, ensuring all temporary and intermediate files are encrypted at rest.

wrongOptionNotes.B: GuardDuty is a threat detection service; it does not automatically modify resource configurations or re-encrypt EBS volumes.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Training artifacts stored on local instance volumes are at rest, not in transit across network boundaries where a firewall would inspect them.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks at the network layer and does not address data encryption on attached EBS volumes.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise AI team is deploying an LLM-powered chatbot on Amazon Bedrock. Security requires that no user session data or prompt history is retained by the foundation model provider for model training or improvement. What configuration ensures this compliance requirement is met?

options.text: Use foundation models available via Amazon Bedrock, which by default do not use customer inputs or outputs to train underlying AWS models.
Enable AWS CloudTrail data events to log all InvokeModel calls and reject any calls containing persistent user tracking cookies.
Deploy the foundation model via Amazon SageMaker JumpStart inside a private VPC with internet access completely disabled via VPC Endpoints.
Route all API requests through an Amazon API Gateway configured with a custom authorizer that strips user metadata.

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock is designed with enterprise security and privacy in mind. Customer prompts and model outputs are not used to train the base models or shared with third-party model providers, fulfilling strict corporate data governance mandates without extra configuration.

wrongOptionNotes.B: CloudTrail logs management and data events for auditing, but does not control or alter model provider data retention practices.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While VPC endpoints secure network transit, data retention terms depend on the specific model deployment choice and service terms, whereas Amazon Bedrock natively enforces zero data retention for training by default.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Stripping metadata at API Gateway does not affect Amazon Bedrock's backend data retention policies for payloads received by the foundation model.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A healthcare startup is building a patient portal backed by Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoints. A security vulnerability scan reveals that endpoint invocation payloads containing Protected Health Information (PHI) are traversing the public internet. What is the correct architectural pattern to secure this traffic?

options.text: Configure Amazon CloudFront with AWS WAF in front of the SageMaker endpoint to encrypt all inbound traffic using HTTPS.
Deploy an Application Load Balancer in public subnets with mutual TLS authentication enabled to terminate client connections.
Access the SageMaker endpoint using Interface VPC Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) from within the client application's VPC.
Configure an AWS Transit Gateway with inter-region peering to isolate the inference traffic from the public internet.

questions.explanation: To ensure sensitive data such as PHI does not traverse the public internet when invoking Amazon SageMaker endpoints, architects should use Interface VPC endpoints powered by AWS PrivateLink. This keeps all network traffic within the secure AWS backbone network.

wrongOptionNotes.A: CloudFront routes traffic over the public internet to reach origin servers, failing the requirement that traffic must not traverse the public internet.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Exposing an ALB publicly still leaves an entry point on the internet, which violates the strict requirement to keep PHI traffic off the public internet.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Transit Gateway manages routing between VPCs and on-premises networks, but it does not directly secure access to SageMaker endpoints from client applications.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An enterprise AI governance board mandates that all fine-tuning jobs executed in Amazon Bedrock must be traceable to specific business units for cost allocation and accountability. Which feature should administrators implement to satisfy this governance requirement?

options.text: Implement AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) that inject department IDs directly into the body of every inference prompt.
Configure AWS Trusted Advisor to automatically scan IAM policies and append department identifier tags to active Bedrock sessions.
Apply AWS cost allocation tags to Amazon Bedrock custom model resources and fine-tuning jobs.
Apply AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) resource shares to associate fine-tuning job ARNs with department IAM roles.

questions.explanation: AWS resource tagging is the primary mechanism for attributing resource usage and costs to specific business units. Custom models and fine-tuning jobs in Amazon Bedrock support resource tagging, enabling granular cost allocation and governance tracking.

wrongOptionNotes.A: SCPs define permission guardrails at the account or organizational unit level; they cannot inspect or modify API payload contents.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Trusted Advisor provides recommendations for cost, security, and performance, but it does not automatically modify resources or apply operational tags.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS RAM shares specific AWS resource types across accounts, but it is not used for tagging or attributing Bedrock fine-tuning jobs to business units.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: A multinational financial services company is setting up automated compliance monitoring for generative AI applications deployed across multiple AWS accounts. The security team needs a centralized audit trail of every time an Amazon Bedrock foundation model is invoked, including who made the call and the exact timestamp. Which service should they configure?

options.text: AWS Config rules evaluating the compliance status of Amazon Bedrock custom model configurations daily.
Amazon GuardDuty malicious IP threat lists combined with VPC Flow Logs.
Amazon CloudWatch Logs metric filters targeting API Gateway access logs for the Bedrock proxy endpoints.
AWS CloudTrail data events for Amazon Bedrock

questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail data events capture API operations performed on or within a resource. For Amazon Bedrock, enabling CloudTrail data events for InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream actions provides a comprehensive audit trail of model usage across accounts.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS Config evaluates resource configurations at a point in time, whereas tracking individual model invocations requires real-time activity auditing via CloudTrail.
wrongOptionNotes.B: VPC Flow Logs track IP traffic metadata, not API-level model invocation details such as user identity and model IDs.
wrongOptionNotes.C: If clients invoke Bedrock directly via SDKs rather than through an API Gateway proxy, CloudWatch will not capture those calls.

questions.domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
questions.question: An AI platform engineer is configuring an Amazon SageMaker pipeline that processes sensitive financial data. Compliance mandates that all intermediate datasets and model weights written to Amazon S3 must be encrypted using a dedicated key managed by the company's security team rather than the default AWS-managed key. How should the pipeline be configured?

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 Bucket Keys on the destination bucket to reduce KMS request costs without specifying a customer key.
Attach an IAM permissions boundary to the SageMaker execution role that forces S3 server-side encryption with AWS managed keys (SSE-S3).
Apply an Amazon S3 Lifecycle policy that automatically re-encrypts objects using customer-managed keys 24 hours after upload.
Configure the SageMaker pipeline execution role with permissions to use a specific customer-managed AWS KMS key (CMK), and pass that key ARN in the pipeline step configurations.

questions.explanation: To enforce strict governance over cryptographic materials, SageMaker pipelines accept customer-managed KMS key (CMK) identifiers in their execution configurations, ensuring all pipeline outputs and intermediate artifacts meet internal compliance encryption standards.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Bucket Keys reduce KMS API calls but do not fulfill the mandate to use a specific customer-managed KMS key for encryption.
wrongOptionNotes.B: SSE-S3 uses AWS-managed keys, which directly contradicts the requirement to use a customer-managed key.
wrongOptionNotes.C: S3 lifecycle policies cannot alter the encryption key of existing objects in place; objects must be rewritten with the target key.
